claims.text: The initial as-cast MnNiSi-based alloy has a homogeneous magnetocaloric matrix.
The initial as-cast alloy contains minimal secondary phases.
Annealing a previously homogenized alloy at approximately 600 °C for 1–2 hours will promote nucleation and controlled growth of nanoscale precipitates.
The tailored annealing will produce ductile second-phase precipitates predominantly at grain boundaries.
The tailored annealing can preserve the primary magnetocaloric matrix.
The grain-boundary precipitates will obstruct crack propagation.
The precipitates will hinder dislocation motion.
Obstructing cracks and dislocation motion will increase mechanical strength and toughness.
Keeping the precipitate volume fraction low and the precipitates well dispersed will leave the main magnetocaloric phase largely intact.
Preserving the main magnetocaloric phase will preserve a large magnetocaloric effect.
The treated alloy will have higher tensile strength than the as-cast baseline.
The treated alloy will have greater ductility than the as-cast baseline.
The treated alloy will retain a magnetocaloric entropy change similar to that of untreated material.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration could produce excessive or coarse precipitates.
Excessive or coarse precipitates could disrupt the magnetocaloric matrix and reduce the entropy change.
Insufficient heat treatment may produce too few precipitates to improve mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The comparison baseline is inconsistent: the predicted outcome is stated relative to an as-cast alloy, the baseline allows either an as-cast or standard-homogenized state, and the experiment specifically uses a homogenized control. Because the intervention itself follows homogenization, these alternatives do not represent the same baseline.
